tasks.evidence: EXP190 transfers quantize_row_q8_K_ref (CPU Q8_K activation quantization) to Goose. It was chosen by measurement, not by guess: the built libggml-cpu.so contains ZERO ymm/zmm instructions in quantize_row_q8_K, so the executed code is exactly the scalar algorithm, and it is registered at ggml-cpu.c:393 (.from_float) so it is on the --cpu-moe path. Full algorithm in Goose: abs-max scan, zero-block early out, -127/max scale, rounding and clamp, the sixteen group sums and the 1/iscale delta. 8 checks/0 failures, byte-for-byte equality of the whole block_q8_K against quantize_row_q8_K_ref from the real libggml-base.so, sizes 256/512/2560/4096 including an all-zero super-block. Two own defects fixed: the float stride (element j is at byte 4*j, not j, which produced every fourth byte) and nearest_int not being roundf (it adds 12582912.f and masks the mantissa: round-half-to-even, unlike roundf). APEX EXECUTION CHECK: NEGATIVE. An LD_PRELOAD shim overriding quantize_row_q8_K_ref was validated standalone (2 calls to Goose, 0 native, byte-identical) and then loaded into a real Apex run: output exact but no witness, and objdump finds no call site to quantize_row_q8_K in libggml-cpu at all. The CPU MoE graph reaches the expert matmul (op=100,42560 calls) and dense matmul (op=40,138 calls) directly, both already covered by EXP143. So the module is byte-exact but off the Apex path, like EXP182 and EXP188. No performance claim. The portable-ISA scope is NOT closed: ggml_vec_dot_q4_K_q8_K has 58 SIMD instructions and ggml_vec_dot_q6_K_q8_K has 91 on this host, Goose has no SIMD, and the compiler documentation places SIMD outside current scope, so the quantized dot families remain native. DUPLICATE FOUND 2026-11-08: EXP190 transferred quantize_row_q8_K_ref, but the Apex log already carries FG148_QUANT kind=9 calls=456800 values=172640 -- EXP148 installed a Goose Q8_K encoder into the CPU type-trait table (source/quant/unit.c:43, kind=9 width 256 stride 292), so the native function this module replaces is unreachable on the executed path. A loaded LD_PRELOAD probe confirmed the negative directly: its wrapper never fired in a real Apex run while the same probe worked in a standalone DSO test. EXP190 is therefore a duplicate of completed work, not remaining scope, and is marked DUPLICATE. Same lesson as EXP188: read the executed implementation, not the first match by name, and check the type-trait table before porting a from_float.
